operations.name: Versioned Report Definition Catalog
operations.description: The system shall support the complete report-definition catalog identified by a controlled, versioned specification artifact. The artifact shall identify each report, its fields, filters, scope, and output rules, and shall include the definitions formerly referenced as Appendix A and Appendix B. The project shall include the applicable catalog version in the approved specification, and acceptance testing shall verify that every report definition in that version is implemented.

operations.name: Consortium Capacity
operations.description: The system shall support consortium operations across at least 286 libraries, 17 million annual circulations, and the purchasing and processing of more than 900,000 items annually. Acceptance testing shall load representative records at these stated volumes and verify that reports can query the full consortium data set without data loss or errors. These figures define the minimum operational scale the system must accommodate.

operations.name: Enterprise Library Automation System Integration
operations.description: The system shall integrate with the enterprise Library Automation System, including its Acquisitions and Cataloging modules, and shall not replace their operational functions. The Library Automation System shall remain the system of record for its data; the reporting system shall read the data required for reporting through supported interfaces or read-only access. The implementation shall document the interfaces, data ownership, supported read operations, and synchronization behavior for each module.

operations.name: Patron Characteristic Filtering and Grouping
operations.description: The system shall allow report users to filter and group queries and reports by patron age range, ZIP code, county of residence, home library, patron type, and preferred language. Patron type shall support categories such as adult, juvenile, senior, and student. Acceptance testing shall verify that each characteristic can be selected as a filter and grouping field and that results reflect the selected criteria.

operations.name: Unfilled and Stale Holds Reporting
operations.description: The system shall provide reports for unfilled holds and stale holds. An unfilled hold is a hold that has not been fulfilled; a stale hold is an unfilled hold that has remained unfulfilled beyond a report-user-configurable age threshold. Report users shall be able to select the threshold and identify which category each result meets. Acceptance testing shall verify that all stale holds are included among unfilled holds and that unfilled holds below the threshold are not classified as stale.

operations.name: Edited Record Counts
operations.description: The system shall provide a report counting records edited within a report-user-specified period. The report shall support both item and bibliographic record types, identify the selected record type and period, and return the count for that type and period. Acceptance testing shall compare the reported counts with a reference set of item and bibliographic record edits.

operations.name: Queued Background Report Processing
operations.description: The system shall queue complex and long-running report jobs and process them in the background, separately from interactive sessions. A report user shall receive job status within five seconds of submission, and the queue shall accept at least 100 pending jobs without blocking submission or interactive operations. Report execution shall not directly block circulation or other interactive operations; acceptance testing shall verify that circulation response times remain within the target specified for online-hours workload continuity. Results for the inactive-patrons report shall be cached for the same parameters and data snapshot, with the cache invalidated when that snapshot changes.

operations.name: Environment Separation and Configuration Migration
operations.description: The system shall provide separate development, training, and production environments so that development and training work does not affect production. Authorized report users shall be able to export and import report templates, saved queries, permission settings, and other report configurations between environments. Acceptance testing shall verify that each artifact type can be migrated and that imported configurations retain their settings and permissions without changing production until explicitly applied.

operations.name: Email Report Delivery
operations.description: The system shall deliver generated reports by email to one or more recipients entered by a report user or selected from an address book. Before delivery, the report user shall be able to review and change the recipient list. The system shall report whether delivery succeeded or failed for each recipient, so report users can verify delivery without relying on an unreported send attempt.

operations.name: Current-Data Reporting
operations.description: For reports designated as requiring current data, the system shall include source transactions committed no more than five minutes before report generation begins. Each report shall display the data-through timestamp. If a source is unavailable or the five-minute freshness target cannot be met, the system shall identify the affected data and its timestamp rather than presenting it as current. Acceptance testing shall compare report contents and timestamps with committed source transactions.

operations.name: Complete Data Specifications
operations.description: The system developer shall provide complete data specifications for authority, bibliographic, order, item, hold, and other records maintained or accessed by the system. The specifications shall identify record and field names, data types, relationships, and which records and fields are available for querying. The documentation shall be delivered with the system and reviewed against the data structures available to report authors, developers, integrators, and data architects.

operations.name: System Accessibility
operations.description: The system, including reporting functions, online help, and HTML report output, shall comply with Section 508 and applicable accessibility standards. It shall support screen-reading software, including JAWS and NVDA, screen-magnification software, including ZoomText, and other assistive technologies. Acceptance testing shall assess the system's user-facing functions against the applicable accessibility criteria and verify access using the identified assistive technologies.

operations.name: Batch Item Status Conversion
operations.description: The system shall allow authorized staff members to select multiple items and change their status in one batch operation, including changing items from missing to discard/weed. Before applying the change, the system shall show the selected item count and the source and destination statuses and require confirmation. Acceptance testing shall verify that the change applies only to the selected items and that items with an invalid status transition are identified rather than silently changed.

operations.name: Anonymized Aggregate Transaction Retention
operations.description: The system shall retain monthly and annual aggregate transaction information indefinitely only after it has been de-identified so that it cannot identify a patron. These aggregates are exempt from the configurable retention periods for identifiable financial and transaction records, subject to applicable law and an authorized legal hold. If law or policy changes require deletion or a different retention period for an aggregate category, the system shall apply the revised rule and record the action.

operations.name: Historical Reporting Data
operations.description: The system shall support reporting on historical data, including billing data as of a specified past date and snapshots of bill amounts on that date. Retention for identifiable transaction history shall follow the configurable periods in the Financial Data Retention Policy, including applicable audit requirements and legal holds. De-identified monthly and annual aggregates shall follow the separate indefinite-retention rule for aggregate transaction information. Reports shall identify the date or period represented by the historical data.

operations.name: Financial Data Retention Policy
operations.description: The system shall enforce configurable retention periods by financial data category, including the required seven-year audit period where applicable. The policy shall distinguish identifiable transactions and financial records from de-identified monthly and annual aggregates; only the latter are exempt from configurable deletion under the aggregate-retention rule. An authorized legal hold shall suspend deletion for affected records, and a policy change shall govern future processing and any existing data as required by law. The system shall record retention-policy changes and deletion actions for audit.

operations.name: Relational Queries and Historical Reporting Architecture
operations.description: The system shall support report queries and joins over the normalized relational data structures of the Library Automation System without requiring a denormalized reporting schema. Historical reporting may use a normalized historical store, snapshots, or a read-only replica; it shall not require maintaining a denormalized copy of live data. The implementation shall document how historical data is synchronized, how reporting workloads are isolated from production transactions, and the data-through timestamp used to indicate consistency.

operations.name: Historical Reporting Store
operations.description: The system shall provide historical reporting for a specified date or date range using a normalized historical store, historical snapshots, or a read-only replica. The chosen architecture shall preserve the source data relationships and shall not require a denormalized reporting store. The system shall identify the data-through timestamp for each report and document how historical data is synchronized and reconciled with the Library Automation System.

operations.name: Isolated Read-Only Reporting
operations.description: The system shall isolate reporting workloads from production transactional operations using a separate reporting database, a read-only replica, or an equivalent architecture. Reporting access shall not modify source records. For historical reporting, the architecture may include a normalized historical store or snapshots; synchronization and data freshness shall be documented, and each report shall identify its data-through timestamp.

operations.name: Normalized Reporting Data Constraint
operations.description: The system shall not require a denormalized copy of production data for reporting. Reporting may use normalized relational structures, a read-only replica, or a normalized historical store with snapshots. Any proposed denormalized store shall require documented justification and approval, including a synchronization plan and consistency checks that prevent the store from presenting stale or inconsistent data as current.

operations.name: Library Capacity Analysis
operations.description: The system shall provide an interface and analysis capabilities for viewing capacity across libraries and assessing collection distribution. It shall aggregate capacity data across libraries by querying the centralized database. Library managers and collection planners shall be able to review inventory and capacity reports for their daily work, including capacity and distribution needs.

operations.name: Library Capacity Overview
operations.description: The system shall provide an overview showing capacity information for all libraries in a library system. For each library, the overview shall display the available capacity metrics, including current load and capacity percentage. Report users shall be able to review the libraries and their metrics together to support capacity and resource decisions.

operations.name: Library Grouping and Filtering
operations.description: The system shall allow report users to group libraries by library system or configured region and to sort and filter them by region, library type, and current load. The overview shall label the selected grouping and filters. These controls shall allow report users to navigate and compare libraries in a consortium-scale overview.

operations.name: Library Comparison View
operations.description: The system shall provide a comparison view that displays selected report breakdowns for multiple libraries side by side. Directors and library managers shall be able to compare the same measures and reporting period across libraries and identify differences. The view shall label each library, measure, and reporting period so the results can be compared without inspecting separate reports.

operations.name: Financial Record Associations
operations.description: The system shall associate fines, charges, waivers, and ecommerce transactions with the relevant patron and item records. Finance staff members and report users shall be able to use these associations when reviewing financial activity. Acceptance testing shall verify that each supported transaction type is linked to the correct patron and item records when those records exist.

operations.name: Demographic Statistics and Privacy
operations.description: The system shall provide demographic statistics to support program planning and analysis of patron demographics and interests. Statistics shall include transactions by geographic region, county, city, ZIP code, and age range, as well as patron and circulation aggregates grouped by demographic fields. The system shall use de-identified data for these statistics and shall not expose patron-identifying information in the reported results.

operations.name: Configurable Inactive Patron Reports
operations.description: The system shall generate a list of patrons with no circulation or electronic activity during a report-user-configurable number of days. Report users shall be able to enter any number of days and select common presets of 30, 90, 180, or 365 days; the report shall support scopes such as library system, home library, and county. The output shall identify the inactivity threshold and the patron records meeting it.

operations.name: Indirect Patron Access to Report Output
operations.description: The system shall allow libraries to display selected report output on screens intended for patrons without providing patrons with access to reporting functions or underlying report data. Patron interactions with library services shall remain primarily through the OPAC. Acceptance testing shall verify that displayed output contains only the information selected for public display and does not expose restricted patron information.

operations.name: Bills and Debt Reports
operations.description: The system shall provide bills reports for staff members and finance staff members. The reports shall include bills currently owed by patrons, detailed payments received, forgiven amounts, payments made using work credit, payments made using goods credit, detailed voids, and aged debt. Each report shall label these categories separately so staff members can distinguish payments, credits, and forgiven amounts when reviewing outstanding bills and payment activity.

operations.name: Financial Transaction Update Latency
operations.description: The system shall reflect a committed financial transaction, including a front-desk payment, in account balances and reports designated as current within five minutes of the transaction commit. Such reports shall display their data-through timestamp. If the transaction is not available within that interval, the system shall identify the affected data as delayed rather than presenting it as current. Acceptance testing shall measure elapsed time from transaction commit to report availability.

operations.name: Editable Financial Information
operations.description: The system shall allow authorized staff members to select a financial record, edit permitted fields, review the proposed changes, and save or cancel the update. The system shall validate required fields before saving and identify validation failures to the staff member. Acceptance testing shall verify that authorized staff members can update permitted fields and that unauthorized changes are rejected.

operations.name: Strategic Planning Reports
operations.description: The system shall provide library administrators, managers, and directors with aggregated reports for strategic planning, evaluation, and service decisions. Report users shall be able to review measures grouped by reporting period and library, and by collection where the measure supports that dimension. Reports shall label measures, groupings, and periods and shall support presentation of the resulting summaries to a library board.

operations.name: Combine Query Criteria
operations.description: The system shall let report users combine query clauses and filters using AND and OR Boolean operators and group clauses. Supported item status values shall include missing, discard/weed, and damaged, as defined by the Library Automation System's status codes. A time-in-status criterion shall mean elapsed time since the item entered its current status; activity criteria shall include elapsed time since last circulation. Acceptance testing shall verify the results of combined criteria against records with known statuses, status-entry dates, and circulation dates.

operations.name: Consolidated Data Completeness and Freshness
operations.description: For each consolidated report, the system shall identify the libraries included, the data-through timestamp for each library, and any source data unavailable to the report. Data shall be considered current only when it meets the five-minute freshness target for reports designated as requiring current data. Acceptance testing shall compare report contents with source records and verify that missing or delayed library data is identified rather than presented as complete and current.

operations.name: Online-Hours Workload Continuity
operations.description: The system shall allow reports to run during open hours without disrupting circulation or OPAC use. Under the consortium workload capacity specified for acceptance testing, the 95th-percentile response time for interactive circulation and OPAC requests shall not exceed two seconds, excluding network latency outside the system boundary. Long-running reports shall be queued and processed in the background. Acceptance testing shall compare interactive response times with and without the representative reporting workload.

operations.name: Large Dataset Report Performance
operations.description: The system shall generate the inactive-patrons report for a dataset containing 3.5 million patron records within 30 minutes when run under the acceptance-test environment and workload. During that run, interactive circulation and OPAC requests shall continue to meet the response-time target for online-hours workload continuity. Acceptance testing shall verify the report results against a reference data set.

operations.name: Report Output Accuracy
operations.description: The system shall produce report outputs that match the selected report criteria and source data. For each release, acceptance testing shall run a defined suite of reports against reference data containing known records, totals, and edge cases; all returned records and aggregate values shall match the expected results. The system shall identify execution failures and shall not present a partial result as a complete report.

operations.name: Board and External Reports
operations.description: The system shall provide predefined reports for library boards and external reporting needs, including the Georgia Annual Report and the Application for State Aid. The approved, versioned report catalog shall identify the required fields, calculations, reporting periods, and output rules for each report and applicable form version. Acceptance testing shall verify each report against that catalog and the corresponding form requirements.

operations.name: Reporting Interface Options
operations.description: The system shall provide three reporting interfaces: predefined report templates, on-demand reports configured for a specific run, and open-template reporting. The interface shall identify which of these modes is being used and provide the controls for selecting or configuring the report accordingly. Acceptance testing shall verify that report users can run a predefined template, change run-time criteria for an on-demand report, and create or configure an open template.

operations.name: Customizable Weeding Reports
operations.description: The system shall provide weeding reports that identify items for review using criteria configurable by authorized report users. Criteria shall include an item remaining in the missing status for more than a configurable number of months and items in the discard/weed status, as defined by the Library Automation System's status codes. Each report shall include the date of the item's last circulation. A report shall identify items for review only; it shall not itself purge or delete items.

operations.name: Approved Report Type Coverage
operations.description: The system shall provide every report type in the approved, versioned report-gap register maintained for the project. The register shall identify each report type and its required fields, filters, scope, and output rules. Acceptance testing shall verify that each registered report type is available and conforms to its entry; report types not listed in the approved register are outside this requirement.

operations.name: Delayed Transfer Alerts
operations.description: The system shall notify specified staff members when an item transfer is delayed or encounters an issue. Notifications shall identify the affected transfer and item, the sending and destination libraries, the delay or issue detected, and the time detected. Acceptance testing shall verify notification when a configured transfer-delay condition or defined transfer issue occurs.

notes: Merged duplicate requirements retain their sources automatically. The delayed-transfer candidate is restored as an operational transfer requirement; the vendor-interface candidates are attached to the retained vendor-interface requirement.
